source_example: Climate change poses a serious threat to global food security.
patterns: pose a serious/potential/direct threat to + noun
collocations: pose a serious threat to public health
common_mistakes: ❌ pose a threat for the environment → ✅ pose a threat to the environment
❌ make a threat to health → ✅ pose a threat to health
usage_note: Dùng cho nguy cơ đáng kể, không dùng cho một bất tiện nhỏ.
writing_example: Excessive reliance on private cars poses a serious threat to urban air quality.
speaking_example: I think social media can pose a threat to teenagers' mental health if it is used excessively.

topic_transfer.Environment: Climate change poses a serious threat to biodiversity.
topic_transfer.Technology: AI may pose a threat to some routine jobs.
topic_transfer.Health: Smoking poses a threat to public health.

source_example: Education plays a significant role in reducing inequality.
patterns: play a significant role in + noun/V-ing
have a significant impact on + noun
alternatives: substantial: more formal and large in scale
common_mistakes: ❌ a significantly increase → ✅ a significant increase
❌ significant on society → ✅ significant impact on society
usage_note: Dùng cho mức độ, thay đổi, tác động hoặc tầm quan trọng; không dùng với danh từ cụ thể không phù hợp như 'a significant dog'.
writing_example: Public transport can play a significant role in reducing traffic congestion.
speaking_example: My parents have had a significant influence on the way I make decisions.

source_example: Governments should make substantial investments in public transport.
alternatives: considerable: close and slightly less formal
significant: can emphasize importance rather than size
common_mistakes: ❌ a substantial many people → ✅ a substantial number of people
❌ substantial money → ✅ a substantial amount of money
usage_note: Dùng với thay đổi, lượng, đầu tư, bằng chứng và lợi ích; không thay thế mọi trường hợp của 'big'.
writing_example: Governments should make substantial investments in affordable housing.
speaking_example: Studying abroad requires a substantial amount of money, so it is not possible for everyone.

source_example: Cities face practical constraints when expanding green spaces.
countability: constraint is countable; it is often plural.
common_mistakes: ❌ constraints to expanding parks → ✅ constraints on expanding parks
❌ practical constrain → ✅ practical constraint(s)
usage_note: Phù hợp với rào cản khách quan như tiền, thời gian, luật lệ hoặc đất đai.
writing_example: Although green spaces are desirable, cities face practical constraints such as limited land and funding.
speaking_example: I would like to travel more, but time and money are practical constraints for me.

source_example: Many countries still rely heavily on fossil fuels.
patterns: rely on somebody to do something
collocations: rely on somebody to do something
alternatives: depend on: close meaning, sometimes stronger
common_mistakes: ❌ rely in technology → ✅ rely on technology
❌ rely on doing something → ✅ rely on somebody to do something
usage_note: Không mặc định mang nghĩa tiêu cực; thêm 'too heavily' hoặc 'excessively' nếu muốn phê phán.
writing_example: Many countries still rely heavily on fossil fuels to meet their energy needs.
speaking_example: I rely on my phone for directions whenever I visit a new place.

source_example: Reducing meat consumption could benefit both health and the environment.
countability: Usually uncountable when referring to consumption in general. Plural 'consumptions' is rare and technical.
alternatives: use: simpler and more natural in speaking
common_mistakes: ❌ meat consumptions → ✅ meat consumption
❌ consume of electricity → ✅ consume electricity / consumption of electricity
usage_note: Không thay thế cho 'shopping' trong mọi ngữ cảnh; nói về tiền thường dùng 'consumer spending'.
writing_example: Reducing meat consumption could benefit both public health and the environment.
speaking_example: I am trying to cut down on my sugar consumption, although it is not always easy.

meaning_vi: chuyên sâu/thâm dụng; ở đây là thâm canh
source_example: Intensive farming can damage soil quality over time.
common_mistakes: ❌ intensive work = simply 'many tasks' → ✅ intensive work means work requiring high effort
❌ intensive agriculture is always productive → ✅ it may increase yields but can harm soil
usage_note: Nhấn mạnh mức độ cao hoặc nhu cầu lớn về nguồn lực; không phải từ thay cho 'very'.
writing_example: Intensive farming can increase food production but may damage soil quality over time.
speaking_example: I took an intensive English course during the summer before university.

source_example: Schools should develop students’ capacity to think critically.
countability: Usually countable for a specific ability or limit; also used in 'at full capacity'.
common_mistakes: ❌ capacity of doing something → ✅ capacity to do something / capacity for doing something
❌ the capacity of students → ✅ students’ ability
usage_note: Ưu tiên cho tổ chức, hệ thống, hạ tầng hoặc tiềm năng; với kỹ năng thường ngày của cá nhân, 'ability' thường tự nhiên hơn.
writing_example: Schools should develop students’ capacity to think critically.
speaking_example: I do not think I have the capacity to work and study full-time at the same time.

source_example: Public transport is a more sustainable solution to urban congestion.
common_mistakes: ❌ sustainable for the environment → ✅ environmentally sustainable
❌ sustain development → ✅ sustainable development
usage_note: Bao gồm khả năng duy trì lâu dài, không chỉ nghĩa 'thân thiện môi trường'.
writing_example: Public transport is a more sustainable solution to urban congestion than private cars.
speaking_example: I try to make sustainable choices, such as carrying a reusable water bottle.

meaning_vi: sản lượng/lợi nhuận thu được; tạo ra/kết quả là
source_example: New farming methods may increase crop yields while using less water.
countability: Countable as a noun: a high yield; crop yields.
alternatives: output: total production of a system
common_mistakes: ❌ increase the yieldings → ✅ increase yields
❌ yield more productions → ✅ yield more produce / increase production
usage_note: Hay gặp trong nông nghiệp, đầu tư và báo cáo; trong hội thoại, 'produce' hoặc 'result in' thường tự nhiên hơn.
writing_example: New farming methods may increase crop yields while using less water.
speaking_example: My small garden does not yield much, but I enjoy growing herbs there.

source_example: Online learning is not equally suited to all students.
common_mistakes: ❌ suited with online learning → ✅ suited to online learning
❌ suited to do a job → ✅ suited to/for a job
usage_note: Không phải lựa chọn tự nhiên khi nói về quần áo; thường dùng 'fit' hoặc 'look good on'.
writing_example: Online learning is not equally suited to all students.
speaking_example: I think I am better suited to working independently than in a very large team.

source_example: Cycling uses a fraction of the energy required by private cars.
patterns: only a small fraction of + plural/uncountable noun
at a fraction of the cost
prepositions: at a fraction OF the cost
countability: fraction is countable; this expression normally uses singular after 'a'.
collocations: at a fraction of the cost
a tiny fraction of the population
alternatives: a small proportion of: useful for statistics
far less: more natural in speaking
one tenth of: precise numerical comparison
common_mistakes: ❌ a fraction than the cost → ✅ a fraction of the cost
❌ a fraction costs → ✅ costs a fraction of what X costs
usage_note: Chỉ dùng khi chênh lệch thực sự lớn; nếu không, 'less than' hoặc 'slightly lower' chính xác hơn.
writing_example: Cycling requires a fraction of the energy consumed by private cars.
speaking_example: Streaming a film at home costs a fraction of the price of going to the cinema.

meaning_vi: làm cạn kiệt tài nguyên / tài nguyên đã cạn kiệt
source_example: Unsustainable consumption can exhaust natural resources.
alternatives: use up: more natural in speaking
deplete: more formal and usually used with resources/reserves
common_mistakes: ❌ exhaust of natural resources → ✅ exhaust natural resources
❌ resources are exhausting → ✅ resources are being exhausted / are depleted
❌ depletion of environment → ✅ depletion of natural resources
usage_note: 'Exhausted' describes people or supplies; 'depleted resources' is the natural phrase for resources that have been used up.
writing_example: Unsustainable consumption can exhaust natural resources and increase environmental damage.
speaking_example: I worry that we are using up natural resources faster than we can replace them.
